section: Linguistic groups of India - language families, Eighth Schedule languages, bilingualism
subsections: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey
Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: According to the 1961 Census, how many mother tongues were listed?
accepted.x: The 1961 Census listed 1,652 mother tongues.
accepted.tq: Direct numerical recall of a census figure.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Census 2011 language data:
1. About 19,500 raw mother tongues were rationalised into 1,369 mother tongues.
2. The 1,369 mother tongues were grouped into 121 languages.
3. The 121 languages comprised 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled languages.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Census 2011 language returns were rationalised into 1,369 mother tongues and grouped into 121 languages, consisting of 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled languages.
accepted.tq: Combine the raw count, rationalised count and scheduled/non-scheduled classification.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s: For purposes of Census language classification, a language generally requires at least how many speakers?
accepted.x: The Census counts a language when it has 10,000 or more speakers.
accepted.tq: Test the exact threshold rather than the broader language count.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s: About how many languages are counted as subsets of Hindi in the Census classification?
accepted.x: About 56 languages are grouped as subsets of Hindi.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related census counts.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s: Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India, conducted during 1903–1928, recorded:
accepted.x: Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India recorded 179 languages and 544 dialects between 1903 and 1928.
accepted.tq: Keep the language count and dialect count in their correct order.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Ethnologue lists 455 living languages in India. The People's Linguistic Survey documents more than 780 languages, while 1,652 mother tongues belong to the 1961 Census.
accepted.tq: Match each survey or source with its distinctive count.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s: The People's Linguistic Survey of India associated with G. N. Devy documented:
accepted.x: The People's Linguistic Survey of India, associated with G. N. Devy, documented more than 780 languages.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the survey and its documented total.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s: The Mother Tongue Survey of India found approximately 19,500 mother tongues, including how many foreign ones?
accepted.x: The Mother Tongue Survey of India identified about 19,500 mother tongues, including 103 foreign mother tongues.
accepted.tq: Test the embedded sub-count within a larger survey figure.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Census language count from the constitutional language count?
o: Only the 99 non-scheduled languages are constitutionally recognised.
All 121 Census languages are included in the Eighth Schedule.
The Eighth Schedule contains all 1,369 rationalised mother tongues.
The 121-language Census count includes 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled languages.
accepted.x: The Census grouped mother tongues into 121 languages, of which 22 are in the Eighth Schedule and 99 are non-scheduled. The 121-language Census count should not be equated with the constitutional list.
accepted.tq: Separate the Census classification from constitutional recognition.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India
B. Census listing 1,652 mother tongues
C. Census 2011 language rationalisation
D. Completion of the Mother Tongue Survey of India in November 2022
accepted.x: Grierson's survey was conducted during 1903–1928, followed by the 1961 Census, the 2011 Census and completion of the Mother Tongue Survey in November 2022.
accepted.tq: Use the earliest and latest events first, then place the census milestones.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the Census 2011 ranking and share of Telugu?
accepted.x: Telugu ranked fourth in Census 2011 and accounted for 6.7 percent of speakers.
accepted.tq: Match rank and percentage instead of identifying the language alone.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s: Which change occurred between Census 2001 and Census 2011 in the ranking of Telugu?
o: It rose from fourth to third position after overtaking Marathi.
It fell from second to fifth position after being overtaken by Tamil.
It fell from third to fourth position after being overtaken by Marathi.
It retained the third position with a higher share than Marathi.
accepted.x: Telugu slipped from third position in 2001 to fourth position in 2011, as Marathi overtook it.
accepted.tq: Test a reversed comparison trap involving rank movement.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding language shares in Census 2011:
1. Hindi accounted for 43.6 percent of speakers.
2. Bengali accounted for 8.0 percent of speakers.
3. Tamil accounted for 5.7 percent of speakers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Hindi, Bengali and Tamil accounted for 43.6 percent, 8.0 percent and 5.7 percent respectively in the Census 2011 ranking table.
accepted.tq: Verify several percentage entries without confusing their rank order.
accepted.sec: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the original Eighth Schedule, the 21st Amendment, the 71st Amendment and the 92nd Amendment in terms of the number of scheduled languages?
accepted.x: The Eighth Schedule began with 14 languages, rose to 15 after the 21st Amendment, 18 after the 71st Amendment and 22 after the 92nd Amendment.
accepted.tq: Track cumulative additions rather than the number of languages added in each amendment.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Amendment)
A. 21st Amendment, 1967
B. 71st Amendment, 1992
C. 92nd Amendment, 2003
D. Original Schedule, 1950

List-II (Language addition or status)
1. Four languages added
2. Fourteen languages initially included
3. Sindhi added
4. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali added

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: The 21st Amendment added Sindhi; the 71st added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; the 92nd added four languages; and the original Schedule contained 14 languages.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure amendment-language pair and complete the code.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: Which of the following languages was included in the original Eighth Schedule in 1950?
accepted.x: Telugu was among the 14 languages included in the original Eighth Schedule in 1950. Sindhi, Konkani and Santhali were added later.
accepted.tq: Distinguish original scheduled languages from later additions.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: The Eighth Schedule is constitutionally linked with which of the following Articles?
accepted.x: The Eighth Schedule is linked to Article 344(1), concerning the Commission and Committee on official language, and Article 351, concerning promotion of Hindi.
accepted.tq: Use the constitutional-provision trap by separating linked Articles from other language provisions.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about English and the Eighth Schedule is correct?
o: English was included in the original Schedule but removed in 1992.
English has never been included in the Eighth Schedule.
English was added by the 92nd Amendment along with Santhali.
English is one of the 22 scheduled languages by convention.
accepted.x: English has never been included in the Eighth Schedule.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between official use of English and its constitutional Schedule status.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: Which of the following committees was constituted in relation to demands for inclusion of languages in the Eighth Schedule?
o: Ashok Pahwa Committee and Sitakant Mohapatra Committee
Rajamannar Committee and Fazl Ali Commission
accepted.x: The Ashok Pahwa Committee of 1996 and the Sitakant Mohapatra Committee of 2003 were associated with the issue of inclusion in the Eighth Schedule.
accepted.tq: Match the issue with the committees specifically associated with it.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding inclusion in the Eighth Schedule:
1. There are no fixed constitutional criteria for inclusion.
2. Inclusion can facilitate interpretation in Parliament.
3. Inclusion provides recognition by the Sahitya Akademi.
4. Inclusion permits an option in the UPSC Indian-language paper.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Other stated benefits include authoritative constitutional translations under Article 394A and access to central development funds.
accepted.tq: Identify the cumulative benefits and the absence of fixed inclusion criteria.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: The 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule cover approximately what percentage of the population's mother tongues?
accepted.x: The 22 scheduled languages cover the mother tongues of approximately 96.71 percent of the population.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the current coverage figure from the earlier 91 percent figure.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Khasi and Garo — not included in the Eighth Schedule
Kokborok — included in the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment
Gor Boli — spoken by Banjaras in several Indian States
accepted.x: Kokborok is not included in the Eighth Schedule and is among the languages for which inclusion has been demanded. The 92nd Amendment added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly matched inclusion claim among pending-demand languages.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: Gor Boli, also known as Lambadi, is primarily associated with which community?
accepted.x: Gor Boli or Lambadi is spoken by the Banjaras, including communities in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Rajasthan.
accepted.tq: Match the language variety with its associated community.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gor Boli or Lambadi?
o: It is an Austroasiatic language written in Ol Chiki.
It is a Tibeto-Burman language confined to the North-East.
It is a Dravidian language with a widely standardised script of its own.
It is an Indo-Aryan language spoken by Banjaras and has no script of its own.
accepted.x: Gor Boli or Lambadi is Indo-Aryan, is spoken by Banjaras across several States, and has no script of its own.
accepted.tq: Separate language family, community, geographical spread and script.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: Santhali, added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment, belongs to which language family and is written in which script?
accepted.x: Santhali is an Austroasiatic language and is written in Ol Chiki, a script created by Raghunath Murmu in 1925.
accepted.tq: Match the language with both its family and script.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: Who created the Ol Chiki script associated with Santhali?
accepted.x: Raghunath Murmu created the Ol Chiki script for Santhali in 1925.
accepted.tq: Use the author-creation trap by linking the script to its actual creator.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding recent constitutional editions is correct?
o: The first digital edition was released only in Bhojpuri and Gor Boli.
Only English and Hindi digital editions were released under Article 394A.
The President released a digital edition in Santhali, with first-time editions also in Kokborok and Kashmiri.
Digital editions of the Constitution were released in Santhali, Kokborok and Kashmiri for the first time in all three cases.
accepted.x: The President released digital editions of the Constitution in Santhali; first-time editions were also produced in Kokborok and Kashmiri.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the principal language from the languages receiving first-time editions.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

accepted.s: A language community seeks authoritative translation of the Constitution under Article 394A, interpretation in Parliament and central development funds. These are principally associated with:
o: Recognition as a non-scheduled Census language
Classification as a dialect under Hindi
Recognition by the People's Linguistic Survey alone
accepted.x: Interpretation in Parliament, authoritative constitutional translation under Article 394A and central development funds are stated benefits associated with Eighth Schedule inclusion.
accepted.tq: Apply the listed benefits to identify the relevant constitutional status.
accepted.sec: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands
